report.summary: Chunk 4 of 8 of markdown.py: defines _classify, _classify_wiki, _content_lines, and a helper for generating unique slugified titles.

handoff.purpose: Define link classification functions and a content line iterator for markdown parsing.

symbols.name: _classify
symbols.note: Classifies a raw href into a DocLink (anchor, external, path, or None for empty).

symbols.name: _classify_wiki
symbols.note: Classifies a [[...]] wiki link body into a DocLink, handling namespaces, anchors, external URLs, and wiki/code links.

symbols.name: _content_lines
symbols.note: Generator yielding (line_index, line_with_inline_code_removed) outside code fences.

symbols.name: out
symbols.note: Local variable in the snippet, not a public symbol.

claims.text: Returns None for something that is not a link at all (empty destination).
claims.why: Function returns None if dest is empty after stripping angle brackets.

claims.text: A Windows drive letter ("C:/x") also matches _SCHEME -- and an absolute local path is not an intra-repo relation either, so classifying it as external is correct, not a bug.
claims.why: _SCHEME is not defined in this chunk; cannot verify the match.

claims.text: Splitting order is Obsidian's and is not negotiable: alias on the FIRST ``|``, heading on the FIRST ``#`` of what remains, so ``[[a#b|c|d]]`` has target ``a``, heading ``b`` and alias ``c|d`` -- the same reading Obsidian renders.
claims.why: Code uses partition('|') first, then partition('#') on the target, exactly as described.

claims.text: ``href`` is set to the destination as written WITHOUT the alias, matching what ``[text](dest)`` puts there: the alias is display text, and a consumer that reads ``href`` (``external_links`` does) must not receive prose.
claims.why: href is assigned from inner before alias is stripped (line 'href = target'), so it excludes the alias.

claims.text: ``[[Code:x]]`` is NOT the namespace; it falls through to the scheme test below and is carried as an attribute, producing no edge.
claims.why: _WIKI_NAMESPACES is not defined in this chunk; cannot verify that 'Code' is excluded.

claims.text: Cross-vault, phase K6, gated on a security review. Recognised so it can never fall through to the note matcher and bind to a local file of the same name; resolved to nothing, counted as deferred.
claims.why: _NS_VAULT is not defined in this chunk; cannot verify the namespace handling.

claims.text: Parsed, carried, counted -- resolved by nobody here. The type layer is a separate module being built in parallel; importing it from the document parser would couple two layers that have no reason to know each other, and answering "does DSSResult exist" without it would be a guess.
claims.why: _NS_TYPE is not defined in this chunk; cannot verify the namespace handling.

claims.text: ``[[#Heading]]`` is an in-document jump. Same reading as ``(#anchor)`` in standard markdown: not a relation between two nodes, so not an edge and not an unresolved link either.
claims.why: Code checks if target.startswith('#') and returns DocLink with kind 'anchor'.

claims.text: An off-repo URL written in wiki brackets is still off-repo. Attribute, never an edge -- the rule does not bend for a different syntax.
claims.why: _SCHEME is not defined in this chunk; cannot verify that the regex matches URLs.

claims.text: Both link scanners share this so "a link inside a fence is not a link" is decided once. Inline code is stripped for the same reason: ``[x](y)`` and ``[[Note]]`` inside backticks are a RENDERING of a link -- documentation about syntax, which this repo's own docs are full of -- not a link.
claims.why: Docstring describes intended behavior; the function is partially shown and its implementation (yielding lines with inline code removed outside fences) matches the claim.

observations.what: The function _classify returns DocLink with href set to the original href parameter, not the processed dest. This may be intentional but could cause inconsistency if href contains angle brackets or leading/trailing whitespace.

In _classify_wiki, the variable 'anchor' is extracted from target after partition('#'), but in the code for namespace == _NS_VAULT, the anchor is extracted from target.partition('#') BEFORE stripping path. This could lead to different anchor handling compared to the general case.

The function _content_lines is defined but its full implementation is not shown in this chunk; only the start of the generator is visible. The docstring describes behavior that cannot be fully verified from this chunk alone.
